summary: ACT (Action Chunking Transformer, ResNet-18 backbone) trains end to end on the public lerobot/pusht_image dataset with zero lines of upstream source changed. Truncated to 300 of the 100000 default steps — a pipeline-viability run, not a converged policy. Two things bite anyone reproducing a framework rather than a script. First, the documented entry point only exists after `pip install -e .`, and an editable self-install makes the tracer treat the whole repository as package territory, so the lineage loses every data and checkpoint edge; the fix is to install the dependency extra, uninstall the package, and import from the checkout. Second — and this is the one that would have shipped an un-rebuildable row — `pip uninstall` leaves `src/lerobot.egg-info/` behind, and because the reproduction puts `src/` on sys.path, `importlib.metadata` reads it straight back as an installed `lerobot 0.6.2`, a version that has never been published on PyPI. Every structural check still passes; only trying to install the recorded environment finds it. Separately, upstream's own wandb logging does not survive substitution by a wandb-compatible tracker: `WandBLogger` is coupled to wandb's exact API in three places — it forwards wandb's `resume=None` default, calls `wandb.log(data=...)` with wandb's keyword name, and calls the wandb-only `wandb.run.get_url()` — the first two of which abort the run outright. So the run is logged via a dedicated evaluation step instead (held-out eval_loss 0.528 over 2742 frames, matching training's own step-300 number). This row was re-captured on 2026-08-08 on a newer capture toolchain that records a materially more complete package set: the download step's recorded environment went from 2 pins to 23, and a fresh clone installing exactly those 23 pins with --no-deps and PYTHONPATH unset now runs that step to exit 0. The earlier record's 2 pins could not — the step's own top-level import was missing from it.
experimentUrlNote: No link. LeRobot ships wandb logging behind --wandb.enable=true, but WandBLogger is written against wandb's exact API surface rather than the subset wandb-compatible trackers implement: __init__ forwards wandb's resume=None default and calls wandb.run.get_url() (src/lerobot/common/wandb_utils.py:110,122), and log_dict calls wandb.log(data=..., step=...) using wandb's keyword name (wandb_utils.py:202). Substitute trackers reject all three. Enabling logging therefore needs real wandb credentials on the training host, which this campaign declines to do. The held-out metric is published as metrics/metrics.json by a dedicated evaluate step instead.
